utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good morning -- sorry, good afternoon, everyone. Could we please have the case called.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-79-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the representation. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Alan Tieger, Anna Richterova, and Willem Wijermars, case manager, for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, I am Stevo Bezbradica, the counsel for Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And we note that the accused is on provisional release, and as far as I understand he is doing well. Isn't that so, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What I intend to do now is to cover the ground which are now have covered by the Senior Legal Officer at the 65 ter conference yesterday just so we are all on the same line. Are we having any technical problems? Good. That's fine. Well, the outstanding motions are some which we hopefully will be able to deal with today. The motion on adjudicated facts is one which the Chamber is presently considering, and we will hope to see that coming out and filed in due course. I can tell the parties that it was my intention to try to have that out in order for the parties to benefit from the decision when preparing their pre-trial briefs, but that was, for various reasons not possible. But we're doing what we can in order to get it out. We have also an outstanding motion from the Defence on his request to have Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic assigned as co-counsel. Just to assure you that that has not been forgotten, and we will also hope to be able to deal with that and file a decision in the near future. We have two motions from the Defence seeking access to confidential material in the Plavsic case and the Mrdja case; and if I'm informed correctly, the decision on the Plavsic case has been filed today and the motion is granted, meaning that you have to have access to confidential material in that case relating to the sentencing judgement and proceeding in that case. And we hope, again, to have a decision also on the Mrdja case out and filed in the near future. And we then also have a -- two motions that are more the matter for decision today. One is a motion from you, Mr. Bezbradica, dealing with a request for the Chamber to apply Rule 73 bis (D), which you filed early this year. And we have received the response from the Prosecution on this, and the Prosecution, I think rightly, points out that this is a matter, i.e., the possibility for the Chamber to request that the Prosecution limits its case that the Chamber could do a proprio motu; however, it's obviously in your right, if you will, Mr. Bezbradica, to file this request and the Chamber's attention to it. But rest assured that we are very much aware of the possibilities which the Rule gives us, especially since this amendment in May last year. However, it's at this stage a bit too early, I think, to walk down that road. We will not at this point exclude the possibility that we will indeed be exercising the rights under that rule, but with this I think, Mr. Bezbradica, we could consider your motion dismissed. We then come to an area which is of more complexity, and that is your motion, Mr. Bezbradica, that the Prosecution did not comply with an earlier decision to file the pre-trial brief according to Rule 65 ter (E), and that again is a motion that you filed on the 2nd of January, 2007. The Prosecution has responded to that. It was also covered in the 65 ter conference yesterday, and if I could just summarise what I understand is the position of the parties is that you, Mr. Bezbradica, would like to see the Prosecution file in its brief also a witness list and a list of exhibits all in accordance with (ii) and (iii) of Rule 65 ter (E), and also you have pointed out that the requirements in 65 ter (E)(i) has not been fully complied with. That is the rule which I would venture is a rule that tries to link the indictment and its counts to the pre-trial brief. The position, if I understand it from the Prosecution - and obviously the parties will have a chance to correct me if I'm doing this in the wrong way - is that you feel that in order to comply with 65 ter (E)(i), there may be an editing necessity. I think the term used was cosmetic changes. Let me say, Mr. Tieger, that I'm -- when I look at the indictment and look at the pre-trial brief, that there seems indeed to be a missing link, if you will, from the counts to the pre-trial brief. The pre-trial brief - and I have to give Mr. Bezbradica that is merit in his observation - the link is missing from the counts and the summary of evidence in the indictment to the pre-trial brief. It's a very nice narrative, and we have appendices to it; but I think in order to fulfil the requirements of (i), there needs to be some editing done in order to make the linkage between the indictment and the ten counts and what is now in the pre-trial brief clearer and also the -- the summary of evidence that goes with each count, which also goes to the difference in responsibility, i.e., the question of whether 7(1) or 7(3) are alleged. When it comes to the question of witness lists and exhibit lists, (ii) and (iii) in the rule, it seems to me you have not supplied that because you felt the order was not clear enough. Well, I would like to -- to feel that this is an honest interpretation of the order and not an opportunity to procrastinate and not fulfil what was, in my mind, a very clear order. You should file the pre-trial brief the 1st of December. If you file something, it missed (ii) and (iii). There was no exception made. I grant you that we had a discussion at the earlier conferences regarding the necessity to find common ground, not only on adjudicated facts, a decision on that, but also when it comes to agreed facts and you advanced that as one explanation why you have not fulfilled the requirement regarding 65 ter (E). Well, that's my understanding on where the parties are on this issue. Anything you wish to add to this, starting with Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Nothing in particular to add. Let me offer a couple of comments quickly. First of all, I appreciate the Court acknowledging that it is giving the Prosecution the benefit of any doubt with regard to the misunderstanding concerning the order, and I can explicitly and formally assure the Court that it was nothing more than that. We're happy to file the witness list and exhibit list in compliance with 65 (E)(ii) and (iii). Secondly, with respect to the first prong the Court mentioned, that is the portion of 65 ter that refers to the pre-trial brief, 65(E)(i), I guess I should say I appreciate the Court's favourable comment about the narrative. We will, of course, comply with the Court's instruction to make the linkage more explicit so that there is no issue concerning either the responsibility of the accused in relationship to particular counts or the portions of the pre-trial brief that refer to 7(3) responsibility, as discussed at the 65 ter conference. The issues raised by Mr. Bezbradica was not the question of 7(1) responsibility in respect of the pre-trial brief, but the issue of 7(3) and we'll focus our attention on that as well in order to make it as explicit as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have to add anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I think then it's clear from what has been said, and now acknowledged, that the Prosecution will comply, not only with clarifying its obligations under 65 ter (E)(i), but also supplement the pre-trial brief with the requirements laid out in 65 ter (ii) and (iii). And the date I had in mind for this fulfillment - and this is to show that we are in a generous mode - I considered first 14 days; but given what I've understood from the 65 ter conference, although you're not writing your pre-trial brief in a vacuum, your grasp of the evidence and witnesses must surely will be well at hand, it still would take you some time. So I'm minded to give the Prosecution until the 16th of February to fulfil all its requirements under 65 ter (E).

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: That means, Mr. Bezbradica, as things now stand, you are to submit your Defence brief on the 15th February. Well, given the order I just laid down, that could not be very advantageous for anyone. So the deadline for you to file your pre-trial Defence brief is now moved forward to the 2nd of March; that gives you 14 days to absorb and digest what is coming now in the completed pre-trial brief. With that, we have technically dispensed with the outstanding motions. What I now would like to turn to is that we have so far had very little success, I would say, on the matter of agreed facts. If I recall correctly, Mr. Bezbradica, it's only paragraph 25 of the indictment that you are ready, on behalf of your client, to note as an agreed fact. I may be misunderstanding in this, but it seems that given what is laid down, both in the indictment and in the pre-trial brief as it now stands, it should surely be possible for you, Mr. Bezbradica, to acknowledge what is in there to a larger agree as nondisputed. This is what this exercise is all about, to try to identify the real issues of the case and where the dispute lies. I'm fully aware, Mr. Bezbradica, that given your normal place of practice being in Australia, which is some distance away from where you had your client, that now and then you could be facing problems of communication with your client. But I had hoped frankly, Mr. Bezbradica, that we should have been able at this point to have more from you in the field of suggestions as to facts that are not contested on your behalf. And maybe if you are more forthcoming in that respect, you could get what you wish from the Prosecution, i.e., the narrowing of the case. To me, it seems that the position that you are taking at the moment - and, again, I may be wrong in this understanding - that you are giving very little and your only request for the Prosecution is to more or less withdraw the whole case. And, obviously, that is not likely to happen unless the parties find some other ground for agreement, and I would like to see more of a spirit in the agreement seeking here, Mr. Bezbradica. I understand from the 65 ter conference yesterday that you intend to visit your client following this Status Conference, and you nod in agreement with my assumption. And I would offer to you that it's important that you not only obviously -- and I'm not telling you what you should do as a counsel. I'm just giving you some reflections from where I sit, that you should not only listen to your client, obviously, but also make clear to him how you view the case, not the least in light of other decisions and judgements that have been handed down by this Tribunal. And I'm referring in particular to the Krajisnik case, which deals obviously with the same theory as this case, and we have other cases, they have been put forward by the Prosecution and will, obviously, be considered by the Chamber when we, as we are now, deliberating on the host of issues brought forward by the question of adjudicated facts. So the question of adjudicated facts and agreed facts are, in a sense, bound together here because they are -- this indictment is not a stand-alone indictment. It has an environment, and I think this environment should encourage you, Mr. Bezbradica, to seriously consider what it is this case from your client's point of view is really about. There must be I would offer as there is taken the narrative from the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, which your client actually could find are not contestable. I pause here, Mr. Bezbradica, in order to give you a chance to comment on what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is true. After this Status Conference, I'm flying to Belgrade and I will stay there a few days. And I am planning with my client to just discuss all these issues, particularly Krajisnik case, and I will pass your message to him in full. And I just can't tell you, but I'm sure that we will consider all -- all these matters and to find out what is the real issue of this case. And I can only advise you maybe same time after this what we can do with this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if that is actually borne out of fruition, mainly that the Defence will find that there are, in contrast to what is now the case, a lot of issues that actually could be put forward under the umbrella of the agreed facts, I'm certain that the Prosecution then would be able to review its position and see whether the case could be somehow narrowed or diminished. And in all lucky circumstances, the -- we would eventually perhaps have a meeting of minds between the parties. I'm not saying that this is a requirement, but of course it would be something that also would be the interest of justice and an interest of your client's interest, Mr. Bezbradica. So with that, I intend to leave the questions of the pre-trial briefs and associated matters only to say again, Mr. Bezbradica, that it's clearly important for you to be able to establish contact with your client other than face-to-face meetings, so we don't have a situation where we sit here perhaps at a Status Conference, which probably will be before the usual one on the 120-day period, depending on where we are on the case, and you lack instructions because you haven't been to Belgrade. So I urge you to stay in contact with your client need be because if you, obviously, have to consult with your client to have meaningful contact with the Prosecution. And I urge both parties to stay in contact after this Status Conference and given what may come out of the meeting with your client. Are you taking that on board, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, everything is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, just to sum up this part, then. As things now stand, we look forward to the full pre-trial brief on the 16th of February, Defence pre-trial brief on the 2nd of March. When we will have a pre-trial conference is yet to be determined, as is the start of the case; but as has said before, at present in this stage of the Tribunal's history, if you will, there is a constant reviewing of the docket and when cases are brought forward. So that's why it's incumbent upon all of us to make sure that this case is brought to completion as regards the pre-trial stage as quickly and as fully as possible. And I'm aware that the dates when pre-trial conference and the start of the case is obviously dependent on other factors, and we will review the situation once we have reached the situation on the 2nd of March when we have the pre-trial brief in hand and review the result of the dialogue between the parties and see when it's suitable then to set the next date for either a Status Conference or maybe directly a pre-trial conference. So that's where we are in the formal frame of this case now. And it's only for me to check whether my information that when it comes to disclosure, the 68 rule disclosure is ongoing and there is nothing I'm told that you need to bring to my attention now, Mr. Bezbradica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Everything is under control and recently I received a few CDs and we have to review all of these. And at this stage, I don't have any problem with that. If I have something, I will address you in due time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bezbradica. Finally then, are there any other matters that we have not touched upon and which the parties need to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I take it nothing from you either, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that brings this Status Conference to a close, and we are adjourned. Thank you.
